properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-17: "please review https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22367v1 this was used in design. Anything we can gleen from here in how to make reflow2 design processes better?"

The paper (read 2026-10-17: the first 100,000 of about 250,000 characters, i.e. the method, results, limitations and lessons; the appendices were not read): Gu, Kemeny, Yelin and Lukin, "Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models". In 7 of 8 tasks, Claude, as the DESIGN agent, found circuits with both fewer Toffoli gates and fewer qubits.
- An INDEPENDENT evaluator judges every candidate: "the LLM has no access to the evaluator beyond the feedback returned after each submission".
- The LLM first proposes "several distinct algorithm families", developed separately with occasional cross-pollination.
- A MAP-Elites archive keeps the Toffoli/qubit trade-off frontier, not one winner.
- The archive records lineage, results and brief insights. The agent "never sees the complete search history".
- Each task is a hand-written spec: boundary, input distribution, representation and accuracy target, with no implementation guidance.
- Large domains are checked by sampling, with a bound: if all k tests pass, then with confidence 1−δ the failure rate ε ≤ ln(1/δ)/k.
- Designs exploit an explicit FAILURE BUDGET: 60 stored branch decisions cover 99.99974% of inputs, against a worst case of 263.

ALREADY SETTLED, AND SO NOT ASKED HERE:
- "verified" is earned by a check that can be re-run (dec:idea-what-drives-a-capability-up-the-ladder-instead-of-somebody-typing-it, 2026-10-13);
- a computed fact counts only through its kept record (req:a-computed-fact-counts-only-through-its-kept-record, 2026-10-17).

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) THE DESIGNER NEVER GRADES ITS OWN WORK. The check that moves a claim is run by something other than the agent that designed it, and the record says who ran it. This goes past "re-runnable" to "separate".
(b) IDEATION AS DISTINCT FAMILIES FIRST. Before a decision cements, a step asks for several genuinely different approaches, recorded as alternatives (cap:fork-alternatives exists) and developed separately before one is chosen.
(c) A FRONTIER, NOT A WINNER: keep the non-dominated alternatives across two or more measured qualities. THIS WOULD REOPEN dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable ("unranked … the human judges in hindsight, not a stored score"). It is not a live option unless @ajs reopens that.
(d) AN ATTEMPTS ARCHIVE. Each candidate tried is kept with its measured result, its lineage and a one-line insight, failures included. Optionally the agent is given a deliberately partial history to avoid anchoring on early directions.
(e) A REQUIREMENT AS A WELL-POSED TASK. Its acceptance states the boundary, the inputs (or their distribution), the representation and the accuracy target, without implementation guidance, and reflow2 can say which of these a requirement leaves unstated.
(f) SAMPLED EVIDENCE WITH A STATED BOUND. A check that samples k cases of a larger domain records k and δ, and reads "failure rate ≤ ln(1/δ)/k at confidence 1−δ". That is evidence, never proof: the line the primes trial drew between 0–39 checked and "every n".
(g) A FAILURE BUDGET ON A REQUIREMENT. An explicit allowed failure rate a design may spend on rare inputs, so a design that exploits it says so and the owner approved it.

PUSHBACK:
- The method needs a CHEAP, AUTOMATED EVALUATOR, which is the paper's own condition: "wherever … correctness and resource costs can be evaluated cheaply enough to sustain many rounds of search". Most designs flo2 holds have none (bhome, SeattleArch, Chris's argument), so (a), (c) and (f) apply only where one exists.
- A metric encodes assumptions (the paper on TQ-cost: "their relative importance depends on the hardware and application"). An evaluator-driven search optimizes what is measured, including what was measured wrongly.
- (d)'s partial history cuts against reflow2's "read the design first". It served exploration in the paper, not correctness, and it risks re-trying what already failed.
- (g) is a hazard in safety or legal domains. It must be explicit and the owner's word, never inferred.
- (b) costs N times the development, and is worth it only where a decision cements.

2026-10-17, @ajs: "I want to keep a clear delineation between what an agent (like Claude does) and what reflow2 does. Of the things that you suggested, are they clearly in the reflow2 arena versus the AI arena?"

The line used to sort them: reflow2 RECORDS, CHECKS STRUCTURE and COMPUTES deterministically from what is recorded. It never generates, searches, runs an evaluator, or judges whether a claim is true. The agent proposes, explores, runs checks and drafts. The owner decides. A served skill is reflow2 TEXT that guides AGENT behaviour, which makes it the grey zone.
- reflow2 cleanly:
  - (e) is a check that the acceptance names its boundary, inputs, representation and target, and says which it leaves out;
  - (f) records k, how the sample was drawn and δ, computes the bound, and always labels it evidence, never proof;
  - (g) is a field that only the owner may set, with the budget spent checked against it.
  The agent or calc only supplies the inputs.
- Split, with the reflow2 half clear:
  - (a): reflow2 records who ran each check and flags a claim whose passing check was run by the claim's own author (provenance, as req:a-computed-fact-counts-only-through-its-kept-record already does). Building and running the independent evaluator is the agent's or a tool's job.
  - (d): reflow2 keeps the archive of attempts, with lineage and results. HIDING part of the history from an agent is a search tactic, so it is AI arena, and it cuts against "read the design first". That half drops out.
- AI arena: (b) generating genuinely different approaches is creative work. reflow2's part already exists (forkable alternatives); at most a skill would suggest it.
- (c): reflow2 could compute a non-dominated frontier mechanically from recorded numbers, but it reopens the settled "alternatives are unranked". The search over the frontier is AI arena.
- The paper's core loop (the model proposes, the evaluator scores, the archive steers the next proposal) is entirely AI arena. reflow2 should hold its record, never run it.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-17: from the evaluator-guided design paper, reflow2 keeps (f) sampled evidence with a stated bound and (g) an owner-set failure budget; (e) was kept, then dropped the same day; the rest stay considered
properties.rationale:
SIZE, PLAINLY (a finding, not a ranking):
- (e), (f): small: properties and a reading. (f) reuses the evidence-not-proof line the primes trial built.
- (g): small to medium: a property, and a gap when a design spends a budget nobody stated.
- (b): small to medium: a skill step and a gap before a decision cements; forks exist.
- (a): medium: who ran a check against who designed, on every run.
- (d): medium: an attempt record with lineage, plus a partial-context mode.
- (c): a reopening of settled intent, @ajs's call.

Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22367v1 (read 2026-10-17, partially, as stated above). Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
